=======================================================================
``-f`` Requiring a minimal overlap fraction 
=======================================================================
By default, ``bedtools intersect`` will report an overlap between A and B so long as there is at least one base
pair is overlapping. Yet sometimes you may want to restrict reported overlaps between A and B to cases
where the feature in B overlaps at least X% (e.g. 50%) of the A feature. The -f option does exactly
this.

For example (note that the second B entry is not reported):

.. code-block:: bash

  $ cat A.bed
  chr1 100 200
  
  $ cat B.bed
  chr1 130 201
  chr1 180 220
  
  $ bedtools intersect -a A.bed -b B.bed -f 0.50 -wa -wb
  chr1 100 200 chr1 130 201

==========================================================================
``-r, and -f`` Requiring reciprocal minimal overlap fraction 
==========================================================================
Similarly, you may want to require that a minimal fraction of both the A and the B features is
overlapped. For example, if feature A is 1kb and feature B is 1Mb, you might not want to report the
overlap as feature A can overlap at most 1% of feature B. If one set -f to say, 0.02, and one also
enable the -r (reciprocal overlap fraction required), this overlap would not be reported.

For example (note that the second B entry is not reported):

.. code-block:: bash

  $ cat A.bed
  chr1 100 200
  
  $ cat B.bed
  chr1 130 201
  chr1 130 200000
  
  $ bedtools intersect -a A.bed -b B.bed -f 0.50 -r -wa -wb
  chr1 100 200 chr1 130 201

==========================================================================
``-s`` Enforcing *same* strandedness 
==========================================================================
By default, ``bedtools intersect`` will report overlaps between features 
even if the features are on opposite strands. However, if strand information 
is present in both BED files and the "-s" option is used, overlaps will only 
be reported when features are on the same strand.

For example (note that the first B entry is not reported):

.. code-block:: bash

  $ cat A.bed
  chr1 100 200 a1 100 +
  
  $ cat B.bed
  chr1 130 201 b1 100 -
  chr1 132 203 b2 100 +
  
  $ bedtools intersect -a A.bed -b B.bed -wa -wb -s
  chr1 100 200 a1 100 + chr1 132 203 b2 100 +
  

==========================================================================
``-S`` Enforcing *opposite* "strandedness" 
==========================================================================
The ``-s`` option enforces that overlaps be on the *same* strand.  In some
cases, you may want to enforce that overlaps be found on *opposite* strands.
In this, case use the ``-S`` option.

For example:

.. code-block:: bash

  $ cat A.bed
  chr1 100 200 a1 100 +
  
  $ cat B.bed
  chr1 130 201 b1 100 -
  chr1 132 203 b2 100 +
  
  $ bedtools intersect -a A.bed -b B.bed -wa -wb -S
  chr1 100 200 a1 100 + chr1 130 201 b1 100 -
  
  
==========================================================================

# Scientific and Format Notes: Genomic Intervals and Spliced Alignments

## 1. BEDTools and genomic arithmetic

BEDTools provides command-line operations over genomic features represented as
intervals. Common workflows compare sequencing alignments against annotations
such as genes, exons, peaks, or regulatory regions. The original BEDTools paper
emphasizes flexible intersection operations over heterogeneous genomic data.

Primary paper:

- Aaron R. Quinlan and Ira M. Hall, "BEDTools: a flexible suite of utilities
  for comparing genomic features", *Bioinformatics* 26(6), 2010.
- DOI: <https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btq033>

## 2. A spliced RNA-seq alignment is discontinuous

An RNA-seq read can cross an exon-exon junction. Its alignment then contains
multiple genomic blocks separated by an intronic gap. The gap occupies genomic
coordinates, but it is not an aligned segment of the read.

BED12 represents this with fields including:

- `chromStart` and `chromEnd`: the outer genomic span;
- `blockCount`: number of aligned blocks;
- `blockSizes`: length of each block;
- `blockStarts`: each block's offset from `chromStart`.

For a record with block sizes `20,30`, the aligned length is 50 bases even if
the outer genomic span is much larger because an intron lies between the two
blocks.

SAM/BAM uses the CIGAR `N` operation for a reference region skipped by a
spliced alignment. BED12 blocks and CIGAR `N` encode the same important idea:
the record has aligned pieces that should not be confused with one continuous
genomic interval.

## 3. Relevant `bedtools intersect` semantics

The documented options relevant to this task are:

- `-split`: treat split BAM alignments or BED12 blocks as distinct intervals
  during overlap analysis;
- `-f`: minimum overlap required as a fraction of the A record;
- `-F`: minimum overlap required as a fraction of the B record;
- `-r`: require the requested overlap fraction in both directions;
- `-s` / `-S`: require same-strand or opposite-strand relationships;
- `-u`: report each A record once if it has a qualifying overlap;
- `-wo`: report qualifying A/B relationships and overlap lengths.
